# Homa

> You can start with what you already know about your child. Homa helps with planning, printable materials, records, and useful next steps.

URL: https://thankshoma.com

## What Homa does

Homa helps a parent see what a child does comfortably and what they are learning now. It can create printable materials, record school hours, and save useful family context.

## Feature pages

- Homeschool planner: https://thankshoma.com/features/homeschool-planner
- Homeschool hours tracker: https://thankshoma.com/features/homeschool-hours-tracker
- Homeschool progress tracker: https://thankshoma.com/features/homeschool-progress-tracker
- Homeschool record keeping: https://thankshoma.com/features/homeschool-record-keeping
- Personalized homeschool practice pages: https://thankshoma.com/features/personalized-practice-pages

The progress report covers ages 2 to 16. A parent answers age-appropriate questions about things they have seen their child do. The report compares those answers with cited national sources. It shows what looks solid, what is growing, and one useful next step.

A separate state section summarizes reviewed homeschool-law sources and shows when they were last checked. It is not legal advice and cannot confirm that a family has met a legal requirement.

Sample report: https://thankshoma.com/onboarding/sample

## What is available

- Parent-led progress reports with optional follow-up questions a parent may try together with a child
- Personalized printable materials that open as PDFs
- School-hour records
- Saved family details and search across conversations available in the account
- Four-week subject plans and a weekday planner view
- Web and mobile apps that use the same signed-in family data

The current planner displays activities across a week. It does not move unfinished activities to new days automatically.

## Boundaries

- Homa is parent-facing. There is no child account or child-facing AI chat.
- A parent may choose to show optional follow-up questions to a child and try them together.
- A parent can save the name of a curriculum and tell Homa what works. Current plans do not follow every curriculum's full scope and sequence.
- Homa can record school hours. It cannot confirm that a family has met a legal requirement.
- The progress report remains free under current product policy. The live site is the source for current access and membership details.

## How the progress report works

1. A parent creates or resumes an account and adds each child.
2. The parent answers questions chosen for the child's age and may choose optional follow-up questions.
3. The report compares the answers with cited national sources. Repeating the same answers produces the same result.
4. The report shows what looks solid, what is growing, and a suggested next step.
5. The parent can inspect the method, sources, and the checklist answers used for the report.

Completion time varies by child and by whether the parent chooses optional follow-up questions. The report uses the answers and saved facts provided for that child. It can describe change over time, but it does not say that a Homa activity caused the change.

## Frequently asked questions

Q: Does Homa follow my state's academic standards?
A: No. The progress report uses national child-development and academic sources. A separate state section summarizes reviewed homeschool-law sources and shows when they were last checked.

Q: Can I use my own curriculum?
A: You can save the curriculum name and tell Homa what works for your family. Current plans do not follow every curriculum's full scope and sequence.

Q: What ages does the report cover?
A: Ages 2 to 16. The questions and expectations change with the child's age.

Q: Does my child use Homa?
A: Homa has no child account or child-facing AI chat. A parent may choose to try optional follow-up questions together with a child.

## Technical notes

- The web application uses Next.js, and the mobile client uses Expo.
- Public marketing and article routes provide server-rendered content.
- The root layout publishes Organization and WebSite structured data.
- Interactive onboarding and signed-in product surfaces require JavaScript.
